html:
The first club of modern polo, founded in 1859 at Silchar in the Cachar district of Assam, in northeast India, by British planters and army officers.

Polo itself is very old. Versions were played in Persia and Central Asia and at the Tang court of China more than a thousand years earlier. In the hills of Manipur, east of Cachar, people played their own form, sagol kangjei, on small native ponies. British tea planters and officers in the area learned the game from Manipuri players and set up a club to play it with rules.

The game spread fast. A club was founded at Calcutta in 1862, officers took polo to England in the 1860s, and the Hurlingham Club in London wrote the first British rules in the 1870s. From there it went to the Americas and across the empire. Silchar, a small town in the tea districts of British India, thus gave the world a modern sport. Manipur still plays its own older game.
sum: The first club of modern polo, founded in 1859 at Silchar in the Cachar district of Assam, in northeast India, by British planters and army officers.
